'''Alexander R. Its''' is a Distinguished Professor of Mathematical Sciences at [[Indiana University – Purdue University Indianapolis|Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis]].<ref name=":0"/> He completed his doctorate from [[Saint Petersburg State University]], then known as Leningrad University, in 1977.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=56812}}</ref> Afterwards, he continued his career as a lecturer at the [[Steklov Institute]] in [[Saint Petersburg]] before becoming a professor at his alma mater. He remained there until 1993, when he assumed his current role at Indiana University. His research focuses on [[integrable system]]s, examining asymptotic analysis of matrix models using [[Riemann–Hilbert problem|Riemann–Hilbert]] and [[Isomonodromic deformation|isomonodromy]] methods, asymptotic analysis of correlation functions related to aspects of theoretical [[Fredholm operator|Fredholm]] and [[Toeplitz operator]]s, and the theory of integrable nonlinear partial and ordinary [[differential equation]]s of [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|KdV]] and [[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé]] types.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://math.iupui.edu/people/its-alexander|title=Alexander R Its|website=Mathematical Sciences|access-date=2017-01-23|archive-date=2019-04-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410120134/https://math.iupui.edu/people/its-alexander|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Awards received by Its over the course of his career include the Prize of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] (1976), the Prize of the [[Leningrad Mathematical Society]] (1981), the Hardy Fellowship of the [[London Mathematical Society]] (2002), the Batsheva de Rothschild Fellowship of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] (2009),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hit.ac.il/acc/eugene.kanzieper/yad8/pages/batsheva.html |title=Lectures sponsored by The Batsheva de Rothschild Fund |website=Random Matrices and Integrability: From Theory to Applications |publisher=[[Holon Institute of Technology]] |access-date=2018-03-13}}</ref> and Fellowship in the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list#i |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |access-date=2018-03-13}}</ref> In 2012, a conference on "Integrable Systems and Random Matrices" was held in his honor at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] in Paris.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.math.lsa.umich.edu/~baik/Past_conferences.html |website=[[University of Michigan]] |title=Past conferences |access-date=2018-03-13 }}<br/>{{cite web |url=https://news.iu.edu/live/news/24248-distinguished-professor-alexander-its-at-iupui |title=Distinguished Professor Alexander Its at IUPUI receives IU President's Medal for Excellence |website=Indiana University |date=2017-11-01 |access-date=2024-03-04 }}</ref>
